Searches of MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CENTRAL and Scopus to March 2023 identified 183 randomized trials with N=22,811 adults without diagnosed conditions.

selected.STUDY_TYPE: Preregistered systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
selected.METHOD: MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CENTRAL and Scopus searched to March 2023; randomized trials categorized by intervention; RoB 2 risk-of-bias assessment; random-effects network meta-analysis.
selected.MAIN_RESULT: Most intervention categories improved well-being versus inactive controls; combined exercise-psychological interventions showed the largest reported network effect among categories in the abstract.

selected.LIMITATIONS: Clinical and methodological diversity, indirect network comparisons for some contrasts, variation in outcome measures, and uncertainty about long-term and cross-cultural transfer.

selected.WHAT_WE_CAN_CONCLUDE: Several structured interventions can raise average well-being compared with inactive controls.

selected.WHY_SELECTED: Topic kayjma3 diplomacy dyal Moroccan crises, text dyal treaty, sovereignty, military force, French-Spanish partition, Lyautey administration, urban transformation, resistance w long-term state consequences. Source base kaykfi b rahat l-feature 1000-1500 useful words.

KEY_EVIDENCE: Treaty signed at Fes on 30 March 1912 established a French protectorate while formally preserving the sultan's religious and civil authority inside a new control structure.
The settlement came after international rivalry and the 1911 Franco-German agreement, not as an isolated bilateral event.
France and Spain then formalized separate zones of influence in November 1912, while Tangier later developed a distinct international regime.
Lyautey became resident-general in 1912 and the protectorate rapidly reshaped administration, military control and urban planning.
Academic work on Fes shows new towns were built beside historic medinas, making urban form part of colonial governance.
CONTRADICTORY_EVIDENCE: Formal continuity of the sultanate should not be confused with full sovereign autonomy under protectorate control.
Colonial infrastructure and administrative changes do not erase coercion, unequal power or resistance.
The protectorate was not one uniform territorial regime because French, Spanish and Tangier arrangements differed.
selected.UNCERTAINTY: Exact balance between continuity and rupture differs by institution, region and period; local resistance and negotiated cooperation varied widely.
selected.CONTEXT: The treaty belongs to the longer Moroccan crises of the early 20th century, European competition, debt and military pressure.
selected.CONFIDENCE: high on treaty date, institutional framework and zone structure; medium on broad causal weighting across diplomacy, finance and military pressure
selected.FEATURE_OPENING_MATERIAL: Wa7d wara9a ttsignat f Fes f 30 March 1912 ma 7yedatsh sultan men l-moshhad, walakin bddlat fin kayna l-quwa l-fi3liya: l-forma dyal dawla b9at, w controle colonial wla kay7dd l-qarar.

KEY_FACTS: French protectorate established in treaty form.
Colonial urban policy created new European-planned districts beside medinas.
TIMELINE: 1905-1911: Moroccan crises and escalating international rivalry.
1911-11-04: Franco-German agreement helps clear diplomatic path.
1912-04: major unrest and violence in Fes follows the new protectorate order.
1912-11-27: France-Spain convention defines Spanish influence zones.
1912 onward: protectorate administration, military expansion and new urban planning develop unevenly across Morocco.
1956: protectorate system ends with Moroccan independence.
INTERPRETATIONS: Legal-continuity reading: protectorate kept formal sultanate institutions and used them as a governing framework.
Colonial-power reading: real sovereignty was sharply constrained by resident-general authority and military force.
State-transformation reading: protectorate reorganized administration, infrastructure and urban institutions in ways that survived beyond 1956.
COUNTERINTERPRETATIONS: Calling 1912 a total institutional zero point ignores pre-existing Moroccan state structures and diplomacy.
Calling it simple continuity ignores coercive foreign control and territorial partition.
Colonial modernization narratives need to be weighed against extraction, inequality and resistance.
MYTH_VS_EVIDENCE: DOCUMENTED FACT: Treaty of Fes was signed on 30 March 1912 and created the French protectorate framework.
DOCUMENTED FACT: Spain received separate influence zones through a later 1912 agreement.
LIKELY INTERPRETATION: preserving the sultanate helped make indirect rule administratively workable.
CONTESTED INTERPRETATION: how much later Moroccan state capacity represents colonial construction versus adaptation of older institutions.
UNKNOWN: one single causal weight that explains why the protectorate became possible exactly when it did.
selected.PRESENT_DAY_RELEVANCE: Kay3awn nfhmou 3lach b3d institutions, city layouts w debates 3la sovereignty w colonial legacy ma ytfhmoush ila bdina ghir mn 1956.
CLAIMS_TO_AVOID: Morocco ceased to have any state institutions after 1912.
The protectorate was purely peaceful administrative reform.
All regions experienced colonial control in the same way and at the same time.
Every modern Moroccan institution was created by the protectorate.

selected.WHY_SELECTED: Work kay7mel literary, autobiographical, sociological w postcolonial layers. Scholarship katn9ach voice, gender, nationalism, space, photographs/peritext, magical realism, cultural memory w risk dyal reading l-harem b stereotype wa7d.

KEY_EVIDENCE: Recent Moroccan scholarship reads Dreams of Trespass as an alternative archive that recovers marginalized female memory rather than only as private childhood recollection.
A 2026 Foucauldian reading treats the harem as a space where authority, surveillance and resistance coexist, rejecting a simple power/no-power binary.
Life Writing scholarship shows peritext and photographs change how the work is framed across language editions and audiences.
Other scholarship reads the text through nationalism, magical realism, postcolonial feminism and the tension between constraint and agency.
CONTRADICTORY_EVIDENCE: The book should not be treated as transparent documentary evidence for all Moroccan women in the 1940s.
Scholars disagree on genre emphasis: autobiography, fictionalized life-writing, literary activism, sociological memory and postcolonial text overlap.
A liberation-only reading can flatten conservative, religious, class and family complexities inside the narrative.
selected.UNCERTAINTY: Genre labels and the line between remembered experience, literary construction and representative social history remain interpretive questions.
selected.CONTEXT: Fatema Mernissi, Moroccan sociologist and feminist, uses childhood memory in Fes during the protectorate era to explore boundaries, household life, public/private space and women's voices.
selected.CONFIDENCE: high on major scholarly themes; medium on any single definitive genre classification

selected.CONTEXT: Protectorate-era Fes, nationalist change, household gender order and later global debates about Muslim women shape reception of the work.
selected.CREATOR_OR_WORK_BACKGROUND: Dreams of Trespass: Tales of a Harem Girlhood appeared in 1994 and draws on Mernissi's remembered childhood while using crafted narrative strategies.
selected.STYLE_AND_FORM: First-person childhood perspective, episodic storytelling, multiple female voices, remembered scenes, symbolic boundaries and a form that sits between autobiography and literary construction.
selected.HISTORICAL_RELATIONSHIP: The narrative places domestic change beside anti-colonial nationalism and social transition in 1940s Morocco without making household liberation identical to national independence.
selected.RECEPTION: The work circulates internationally and has generated scholarship on gender, nationalism, autobiography, translation, images and cultural memory.
selected.CRITICISM: Editors should avoid presenting one Fes household as a universal model of Moroccan or Muslim women's experience; class, region, family form and literary mediation matter.
COMPETING_INTERPRETATIONS: Feminist resistance narrative centered on agency against patriarchal boundaries.
Postcolonial multiple-critique reading aimed at both local patriarchy and Western Orientalist simplification.
Life-writing reading focused on memory, translation and peritext.
Cultural-memory reading where women's stories operate as alternative archives.
selected.LATER_INFLUENCE: The book remains a reference point in scholarship on Moroccan women's writing, Islamic feminism, postcolonial life-writing and representation of domestic space.
selected.WHY_IT_MATTERS_TODAY: Kay3llmna kifach n9raw story 3la gender bla ma n7wloha la stereotype Orientalist la slogan wa7d 3la liberation.
CLAIMS_TO_AVOID: The text is a literal documentary record of every event it narrates.
